text:
maria: Quick data point — yesterday at ~09:10 we saw steady KV cache memory growth on the longctx cluster. It only shows up for sessions that keep appending (10k+ tokens). Flamegraph points at many small live allocations from prefix shards.
kevin: That matches the offline trace I pulled. Fragmentation + lots of tiny allocations when we do the sparse-prefix coalescing pass. p99 latency didn't spike but resident set kept climbing.
ashwin: Do we have an example cache key pattern for the problematic prefixes? I want to check hash distribution.
maria: Example key format we're using right now:
```
key = tenant_id || "|" || session_id || "|P" || prefix_fingerprint
```
The fingerprint is 64-bit SipHash output. Suspect collision-avoidance salt is not applied for multi-tenant traffic, leads to asymmetric bucket loads.
rachel: Could also be related to how we currently shard the KV LRU lists — we use 32 stripes. If fingerprint entropy is low for some tenants the stripes become imbalanced, causing local eviction thrash.
samir: CI run #3421 reproduced a similar growth locally. I attached a small script that replays a 50k-token chat with 2x prefix overlap. Observed >20% more page faults vs baseline.
ci-bot: build/3421: replay script completed, logs uploaded -> https://internal-artifacts/replay/3421/logs
kevin: Two hypotheses:
  1) Hash sparsity: SipHash seeded odd (tenant salt missing) -> uneven bucket occupancy.
  2) Prefix coalescing logic creates many tiny fragments in the arena allocator -> fragmentation + slower reclamation.
maria: Short experiment plan:
  - A: Re-roll key to include tenant salt v2: `tenant_salt || tenant_id || session_id || prefix_hash_v2` and test stripe distribution.
  - B: Increase stripe count to 256 for a canary subset to see eviction balance impact.
  - C: Change arena bucket policy: coalesce fragments >512B into shared chunk and measure RSS.
  - D: Add TTL-based soft eviction for prefixes older than 30s unless referenced by active session.
ashwin: For A, I'll implement salt v2. Quick benchmark: run 10k synthetic prefixes across 10 tenants and compute stddev of stripe counts.
rachel: For B, beware of locking costs. 256 stripes might increase contended CAS ops for hot shards. We can do dynamic stripe selection per tenant.
samir: For C, do we have jemalloc tuning knobs to reduce fragmentation? Maybe tcache / lg_chunk tuning could help. But that affects entire process.
kevin: Also note — recent kernel update on worker-images changed madvise behaviour (we switched hints to DONTNEED -> more physical reclaim) which may have exposed fragmentation. Ops said they rolled that on Mar 10.
ops-bot: deploy-ops: kernel 5.15.0-rcx -> changed MADV flags on the image base for perf testing (rolled 2026-03-10).
maria: Good catch. So we might be seeing interaction between allocator fragmentation and kernel reclaim behavior. Need to separate variables.
ashwin: Proposed minimal repro matrix:
  - baseline image + old key fmt
  - baseline image + salt v2 key
  - new image (madvise change) + old key
  - new image + salt v2
  each with stripe=32 vs stripe=256 and arena coalescing on/off.
kevin: Metrics to track: RSS, minor/major page faults, eviction rate, prefix hit ratio, per-shard occupancy stddev, p99 request latency, allocation backtraces (sampled).
maria: I pushed a small patch that logs prefix fingerprint -> stripe mapping for a 30s window. Link: https://phabricator/redwood/PR/6789
rachel: Once we have stripe mapping we can produce a heatmap by tenant and see if a single tenant dominates a few stripes.
samir: If salt v2 fixes distribution that's low-risk and quick. If not, fallback: enhance key to include highbits of content-hash (expensive though).
kevin: Action items:
  - ashwin: implement salt v2 + unit tests (ETA: EOD)
  - samir: add jemalloc tcache experiment matrix and run with replay script (ETA: tomorrow)
  - rachel: run stripe=256 canary in k8s dev (ETA: today)
  - maria: collect pre/post flamegraphs and upload
  - ops: confirm kernel madvise rollout window and any other image diffs
maria: Also adding a short-term mitigation: limit prefix cache growth per-session to 128 entries with LRU demotion. Will push feature-flagged patch.
kevin: Nice. If we limit per-session residency we should watch hit ratio regressions — add a quality check with our eval prompts.
rachel: I'll wire up a dashboard: per-tenant stripe occupancy, eviction rate, per-session cache size distribution.
ashwin: If anyone wants the local replay script: `tools/replay/longctx_replay.py --tokens 50k --tenants 10 --overlap 0.6`
maria: Thanks all. Let's keep updates in this thread so we can correlate logs with phabricator PRs. :thumbsup:
kevin: Agree. I'll post a short summary once we have initial stripe heatmaps.
